Human Trafficking Awareness
Human trafficking is one of the fastest-growing crimes in the nation. Children are frequently being victimized in their own homes, often via the internet. It’s happening in communities across the country and the Commonwealth, and it’s happening right here at home.
Please take some time to learn more about human trafficking in our digital world and how you can help protect potential victims.

Owlett to Host Human Trafficking Education, Awareness Event
September 21, 2026
WELLSBORO – Continuing his efforts to ensure the community is equipped to fight back against human trafficking, Rep. Clint Owlett (R-Tioga/Bradford) is hosting an education and awareness event at 7 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 29, at North Street Community Church in Canton.
“Human trafficking is one of the fastest-growing crimes in the nation, and it is happening here in the Northern Tier,” Owlett said. “My goal is to help people understand what human trafficking looks like so we can put a stop to it. The only way to end this devastating and heartbreaking crime is to work together.”
When people hear about human trafficking, many think about abduction, smuggling or confinement. Owlett emphasized that is NOT the most common form of trafficking happening in the Commonwealth. Instead, it is children who are being groomed and exploited online right in their own homes.
“The human trafficking education sessions we hosted last year opened a lot of people’s eyes about this crime. I even had a grandmother tell me later what she learned helped save her granddaughter’s life, as the girl was being groomed by a man who was ultimately arrested and locked away,” Owlett said. “I hope others will come out to this event and learn more about how to protect their loved ones and neighbors.”
Speakers at the session include Joe Peters, Wyoming County district attorney; and Korrin Moon, president and founder of Lantern Rescue.

title: Owlett, Pickett, Yaw Announce State Grants for Tioga, Bradford County Projects
raw_text:
Owlett, Pickett, Yaw Announce State Grants for Tioga, Bradford County Projects
September 15, 2026
HARRISBURG - Reps. Clint Owlett (R-68) and Tina Pickett (R-110) and Sen. Gene Yaw (R-23) today announced more than $2.3 million in Local Share Account (LSA) grants have been approved by the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) to support water and wastewater infrastructure, road maintenance, public safety and emergency preparedness projects in Tioga and Bradford counties.
Local Share Account grants are funded through gaming revenues under Act 71 of 2004 and support economic development, community improvements and projects that enhance the quality of life for Pennsylvania residents.
“These investments will help communities address needs that are essential to the safety and well-being of their residents,” said Owlett. “Reliable water and wastewater systems, safe roads, dependable municipal equipment and strong emergency services are things people count on every day. This funding will help our local communities make necessary improvements, replace aging equipment and be better prepared when emergencies arise.”
“These investments fulfill a critical funding need for our municipalities and support community projects that residents of Bradford County, and the entire Northern Tier, want to see,” Pickett said. “I am pleased Rep. Owlett, Sen. Yaw and I were able to back these investments and I applaud our municipal leaders for their consistent efforts to strengthen our region.”
“These investments address some very practical needs in our communities,” Yaw said. “Replacing aging wastewater infrastructure, improving road maintenance, providing police and public works crews with the equipment they need and protecting an important historic property will strengthen local services and help ensure these assets serve residents for years to come. I was pleased to join Rep. Owlett and Rep. Pickett in supporting these projects.”
“This project is critical to protecting the Troy Sale Barn and ensuring this historic community gathering place can continue serving the region for another 100 years,” said the Troy Sale Barn Board of Directors. “The partnership between the Troy Sale Barn Operating Corporation, the Troy Municipal Authority and numerous community partners have been essential to preserving and maintaining the barn. This strategic investment would not have been possible without the support of our elected officials. We are incredibly grateful to Sen. Yaw and Rep. Owlett for their continued support of the Troy Sale Barn and their commitment to strengthening our communities.”
“On behalf of the Tioga County Board of Commissioners, we want to thank Sen. Yaw and Rep. Owlett for their continued support of Tioga County and their advocacy for these important projects,” said Marc Rice, Tioga County commissioner. “These LSA awards represent meaningful investments in our communities, supporting critical public infrastructure, law enforcement, and the needs of our local municipalities. We are grateful to see these much-needed resources invested here in Tioga County and appreciate the strong partnership we have with our state legislators as we continue working together to move these important projects forward.”
“These funding awards will have a meaningful and lasting impact by supporting critical infrastructure improvements, police vehicle purchases and truck purchases,” said Daryl Miller, Doug McLinko and Zachary Gates, Bradford County commissioners. “Local governments often face significant financial constraints, and the leadership and advocacy shown by Reps. Owlett and Pickett to help ensure our municipalities have the resources needed to serve residents effectively and responsibly. We are grateful for your continued commitment to rural communities and for working collaboratively to bring these grants to our county.”
The approved projects include:
•
Athens Borough – $67,150
to purchase a new police interceptor vehicle to replace an existing decade-old patrol vehicle that has persistent and expensive mechanical issues. The project includes the purchase of a vehicle, upfitting and custom graphics.
•
Central Bradford Progress Authority, on behalf of Troy Municipal Authority and Troy Sale Barn Operating Corporation – $465,986
to replace a deteriorated retaining wall behind the historic Troy Sale Barn in Troy Borough. The project includes demolition of the failed dry-laid fieldstone wall, construction of a new reinforced concrete retaining wall, drainage improvements and site restoration. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•
Columbia Township – $125,370
to purchase and upfit a new utility truck to replace an aging 2016 maintenance vehicle that has experienced significant rust, frequent breakdowns and approximately $18,000 in repairs over the past three years. The new truck will improve public works operations and allow the township to clear roads more efficiently during snow events and severe weather. LSA funds will be used for vehicle purchase and upfit costs.
•
Lawrenceville Borough – $385,025
to make electrical improvements at the municipal water treatment plant. The project will replace and relocate electrical components that have been damaged by chlorine and moisture exposure, improving the reliability of the treatment facility. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•
Liberty Area Municipal Authority – $218,700
to make improvements at the wastewater treatment plant, including new sand media, distribution piping and a chemical mixer system. The upgrades will improve treatment operations and help the facility remain in compliance with permitting and regulatory standards. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•
Mansfield Borough – $56,375
to purchase a new marked police patrol vehicle equipped with police equipment. The vehicle will strengthen the borough’s limited patrol fleet, improve response times and enhance officer and community safety. LSA funds will be used for vehicle purchase.
•
Rome Township – $335,043
for the reclamation and reconstruction of Robinson Road from North Rome Road to the top of the hill. Funding will support the full-depth reclamation of existing sealcoat surface to reuse the existing materials as part of the new road structure. Following reclamation, an additional subbase layer will be added and new sealcoat will be applied.
•
Tioga County – $250,000
to improve water security in Nelson Township by adding a backup water well, relocating water intake controls, replacing aging valves and installing greensand filtration systems. The improvements will provide a more reliable source of potable water and strengthen the county’s ability to maintain service during emergencies and severe weather. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•
Towanda Borough – $44,030
for the purchase of a specialized manhole repair and removal tool to improve the efficiency, safety and quality of municipal infrastructure maintenance operations. The purchase of this equipment will help prevent injuries, delays and improper repairs which can lead to water intrusion, road damage and public safety concerns.
•
Ward Township, on behalf of the Blossburg Volunteer Fire Department – $176,003
to purchase new mobile and portable radios. The new digital, P-25-compliant equipment will replace outdated radios that are increasingly difficult and costly to repair, improving communications and reliability for emergency responders.
•
West Burlington Township – $28,200
to purchase and install two emergency generators, one at the municipal building and one at the township garage. The generators will maintain essential township operations and provide emergency power to facilities that serve as warming shelters during power outages and severe weather.
•
Windham Township – $200,000
to purchase a new 4WD heavy-duty truck with a plow to be used for the maintenance of the streets and roads. The vehicle will replace the existing 20 year-old truck. It will also be used to haul stone materials to project areas.
The CFA is an independent agency responsible for administering state investments that promote economic growth, infrastructure development and community revitalization throughout Pennsylvania.

Owlett to Host Breakfast Honoring Area Veterans
September 8, 2026
TROY – Rep. Clint Owlett (R-Tioga/Bradford) is inviting area veterans to his upcoming Veterans Appreciation Breakfast on Thursday, Oct. 15, in Troy.
The free breakfast will begin at 9:30 a.m. at the Troy Sale Barn, 50 Ballard St., Troy. Doors open at 9 a.m.
“Our veterans are an inspiring group of people who remain humble despite their extraordinary acts of service for us and our nation,” Owlett said. “Whether they served in times of war or times of peace, these men and women stepped up and helped shape our nation into what it is today.
“This breakfast is just a small token of appreciation for that service,” he added.
Breakfast speakers include Erwin “Butch” Baker, who was drafted into the United States Army in July 1967 and served until July 1969. During 1968-69, he served in the Vietnam War as a member of the 299th Combat Engineer Battalion. Baker attained the rank of sergeant (E-5) and served as a combat engineer, where they built and maintained roads, bridges, airstrips and other essential facilities.
Also speaking will be Tioga County Commissioner Sam VanLoon, a combat veteran with over 22 years of service in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard. He began his career in August 2000 and was assigned to Charlie Company 3rd of the 103rd Armor in Mansfield. In 2013, he transitioned from the Armor community to become a Blackhawk helicopter pilot for the PA Army National Guard. He has deployed overseas four times in support of both Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Iraqi Freedom.
The breakfast is open to veterans of the 68th Legislative District, along with one guest each. RSVPs are required to ensure there is enough food for everyone. To reserve a seat, contact Owlett’s offices in Wellsboro (570-724-1390) or Troy (570-297-3045), or sign up online at

title: Tioga County Awarded State Planning Grant, Lawmakers Say
raw_text:
Tioga County Awarded State Planning Grant, Lawmakers Say
September 1, 2026
HARRISBURG – Tioga County has been awarded a $50,000 state grant to update its countywide comprehensive plan, Rep. Clint Owlett (R-Tioga/Bradford) and Sen. Gene Yaw (R-23) announced today.
Tioga County will use the funds to commission the preparation of a county-wide comprehensive plan. Updates to land use mapping, the Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance (SALDO) and zoning language to provide to municipalities will help ensure alignment with land use best practices. The update will also build upon the county's recently completed housing study by translating the identified needs into implementable land use, zoning and development strategies.
“It is so important for our communities to have big-picture plans in place to guide growth and development while preserving everything we love about living in the Northern Tier,” Owlett said. “I appreciate all the work our county officials put into their planning efforts, and this grant will help them continue that work so our communities are well prepared for what’s ahead.”
“This funding will help Tioga County take a closer look at its housing, development and infrastructure needs and plan for the future,” Yaw said. “A strong comprehensive plan will guide local leaders, support smart decision-making and create opportunities that help keep Tioga County a great place to live and work.”
“We are thankful for the support of Senator Yaw and Representative Owlett in securing this funding for Tioga County,” said Tioga County Commissioners Marc Rice, Sam VanLoon and Shane Nickerson. “This is an important first step in updating our comprehensive plan and taking a thoughtful approach to how our county grows and develops in the years ahead. Through this process, we will work to better understand the priorities of our communities, identify future opportunities and plan for the long-term success of Tioga County. We look forward to working closely with our municipalities and residents to develop a plan that reflects the needs and priorities of Tioga County.”
The funding was awarded through Pennsylvania’s Municipal Assistance Program (MAP), administered by the Department of Community and Economic Development. MAP funding can be used to provide technical assistance to municipalities and other eligible applicants for activities including community planning and implementation.

HARRISBURG
– State Sen. Gene Yaw (R-23) and State Rep. Clint Owlett (R-68) today announced two area businesses have received grants in the second round of funding awarded through the state’s Agricultural Innovation Grant Program.
“Funding from this first-of-its-kind program will give our local farmers and agribusinesses access to cutting-edge technologies and sustainable practices to enhance their operations and increase efficiency,” Yaw said. “I’m pleased to see this significant state investment in our region’s agriculture sector.”
“It is so exciting to see the hardworking folks in our agriculture industry adapting, growing and thriving through innovation,” Owlett said. “Technology has created a lot of opportunities for our farmers and agribusiness leaders, and I’m pleased to see some of our local innovators receive these well-earned investments from the Commonwealth.”
In Tioga County, Woodland Biomass Innovations was awarded $305,035 toward its woody biomass-to-gasoline conversion facility. The company received $50,000 through the program last year for site planning for the facility.
In Bradford County, Cummings Lumber Company was awarded $129,800 toward its automated lumber-handling system.
The Agricultural Innovation Grant is distributed by the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture. The program helps farmers and other agriculture businesses implement new agricultural technologies, conservation, and renewable energy innovations – expanding their potential to generate profits, enrich soil and water resources, and produce energy on the farm.

“High quality athletic facilities support student success, encourage physical wellness and strengthen community pride while helping districts remain competitive,” Yaw said. “This investment will benefit students, families, residents and visitors for years to come and I’m pleased to have worked with Rep. Improvements include a new multi-use turf field with sport-specific markings, modern field lighting and a six-lane track surrounding the fields. Security fencing will also be constructed and installed at each high school.
The project also includes the rehabilitation of the tennis courts at Cowanesque Valley High School and a new softball field with fencing, bleachers and a press box at Williamson High School. Additionally, funding will be used to replace deteriorating playing surfaces, install ADA-compliant bleachers, upgrade field lighting to energy-efficient systems and enhance restroom facilities.

“The budget we were presented with and passed yesterday resolved critical concerns we had when the governor introduced his proposal in February. This budget brought spending down to $50.8 billion while avoiding new taxes for Pennsylvanians and leaving the state’s Rainy Day Fund intact. However, this was certainly not a budget we would have written ourselves and demonstrates how compromise serves an imperative role in the budgeting process.

A $10 million investment in career and technical schools and retaining the Educational Improvement Tax Credit program demonstrates the Commonwealth’s dedication to school choice – supporting our children and the next generation of Pennsylvanians.

“As important as what is in the budget are the items that were dropped from the governor’s original plan, including the legalization of recreational marijuana and an exorbitant tax on skill games which are vital to supporting clubs and small businesses in our communities.
“Of course, there are things we would have liked to have seen included in the budget agreement, such as support for our emergency services departments that are struggling to continue their life-saving mission, and the permitting changes we need to empower our communities to protect themselves against extreme flooding as we just experienced last week. We will continue to advocate for these initiatives until they come to fruition.
“No budget is perfect, and what we’re seeing this year is no exception. Although we were able to bring spending significantly down from the original proposal, it is still beyond what we would like to see for Pennsylvania. – With ATV riding season underway, Reps. Clint Owlett (R-Tioga/Bradford) and Martin Causer (R-Cameron/McKean/Potter) are highlighting the latest cooperative effort to ensure the best riding experience on the popular Northcentral Regional ATV Trail (NRAT).
After identifying an issue with trail access to the borough of Galeton last month, the representatives joined with local leaders and officials with the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) and the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) to identify an alternate route.
DCNR confirmed this week Route 144 from Button Hollow Road has been approved by authorities for inclusion in the NRAT, establishing a 2.75-mile connection to the town.
“The NRAT offers nearly 1,000 miles of the best riding in the Commonwealth thanks to great partnerships between state agencies, local officials and private landowners,” the lawmakers said. “We commend officials in the region and at the state level for coming together once again to find a solution that will keep Galeton connected to this great recreational and economic opportunity. With the nation’s 250th birthday just a month away, riders will surely be headed to Galeton for some great fireworks!”
The lawmakers acknowledged concerns raised by some officials and residents about enforcement, noise and dust suppression.
“While we welcome everyone to the trails to enjoy all our region has to offer, it’s important for all riders and passengers alike to be responsible, respectful, and follow the rules and traffic laws in our communities,” they added.
Permits are required to ride the NRAT. For maps and additional information about the trail, visit www.DCNR.pa.gov and search for the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail.

title: Yaw, Owlett: $36,000 in NAP Funding Awarded in Tioga County
raw_text:
Yaw, Owlett: $36,000 in NAP Funding Awarded in Tioga County
October 21, 2026
HARRISBURG – State Sen. Gene Yaw (R-23) and State Rep. Clint Owlett (R-68) today announced $36,000 in funding to assist low-income individuals, combat food insecurity and improve distressed areas in Tioga County was awarded through the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development’s (DCED) Neighborhood Assistance Program (NAP).
“The Neighborhood Assistance Program allows businesses, communities and organizations to work together to revitalize our neighborhoods and improve access to job opportunities, quality education and affordable housing,” Yaw said. “I appreciate working with Rep. Owlett to support these worthy projects in Tioga County.”
“It’s always a good day when we have the opportunity to invest in our communities, and this funding supports two very important initiatives that improve both public safety and quality of life in our region,” Owlett said. “I was happy to work with Sen. Yaw to advocate for these projects and support the great work being done by Crary Hose Company and the Tioga County Homeless Initiative.”
Crary Hose Company was awarded $27,000 for the expansion of their fire training center to include fire simulation capabilities. Additionally, the Tioga County Homeless Initiative in Mansfield was awarded $9,000 to help address chronic homelessness in its service area.
The funding was part of over $71 million awarded to 443 statewide projects through NAP, which provides tax credits to businesses that contribute to nonprofit organizations’ efforts to revitalize communities. Through the NAP, businesses can receive tax credits of up to 95% on the contributions they make to a qualifying community project. Legislation to expand the NAP was sponsored by Yaw and State Sen. Nick Miller (D-14) and included in the 2024-25 state budget.
